# Synthetic prose corpus

All works and creators in this fixture are invented for testing. Paragraph labels are
source locations, not part of the prose. Nia Vale is a fictional creator. These three
short works cannot establish a complete author profile.

## S1. The station clock

Creator: Nia Vale. Medium: prose vignette. Use all three paragraphs.

S1.P1: The station clock lost four minutes every afternoon. Mara checked it against
her watch, wrote the difference on a receipt, and tucked the receipt behind the glass.
By Friday there were five receipts. The clock still had its brass frame.

S1.P2: A passenger asked whether anyone planned to repair it. Mara showed him the
request number. He copied it onto his ticket. Neither of them called this progress.

S1.P3: On Monday the repairer came with a ladder and a small box of parts. Mara took
down the receipts. She kept the ladder steady.

## S2. The borrowed kettle

Creator: Nia Vale. Medium: prose vignette. Use all three paragraphs.

S2.P1: Tomas returned the kettle with its cord wound around the handle. He had cleaned
the outside, the lid, and the little mesh filter he had not known was there. The dent
remained.

S2.P2: His neighbor turned it over. "It was there when I lent it to you," she said.
Tomas loosened the cord. Then wound it again.

S2.P3: They tried it at the kitchen socket. It boiled. The neighbor filled two cups
and asked whether he wanted sugar. He stayed until the cups were empty.

## S3. Workshop notice

Creator: Nia Vale. Medium: practical notice. This is a contextual exception to the
vignettes' indirect presentation of feeling.

S3.P1: The workshop closes at six on Friday. Please return borrowed tools by five so
we can check them before locking the cupboard. If a tool is damaged, leave a note
with it. We need to know what to repair.
